Answer: B
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, dense curvilinear calcification outlining the cardiac silhouette, particularly along the anterior and inferior borders, which is the pathognomonic radiographic sign of constrictive calcified pericarditis. While the report generator did not explicitly identify this finding, visual inspection confirms the "eggshell" calcification pattern characteristic of this diagnosis, distinguishing it from valvular or annular calcifications.
